title: Genistein alleviates skin inflammation in atopic dermatitis by inhibiting mast cell degranulation through toll-like receptor.
authors: Du, Hongfen; Wang, Na; Wang, Chao; Luo, Shiqiong; Ji, Xiaolan; Li, Rui; Wang, Yuejin; Lai, Xiurong; Li, Henan; Ding, Yuanyuan; An, Hongli
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究染料木素通过靶向TRAM蛋白抑制肥大细胞脱颗粒缓解特应性皮炎，虽含分子对接但核心是蛋白-小分子互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a mast cell-driven inflammatory disorder with limited treatment options. This study aimed to explore the therapeutic potential and mechanism of the natural compound genistein against AD. OBJECTIVE: We investigated the efficacy of genistein treatment on atopic dermatitis and the underlying immune mechanism of cytokine release by mast cell. METHODS: We employed an MC903-induced murine AD model and LAD2 human mast cells. Evaluations included behavioral assessment, serological, histopathology, mast cell degranulation assays, RNA-seq, molecular docking, SPR, pathway analysis, and functional validation via TRAM mutagenesis and rescue experiments. RESULTS: Genistein alleviated ear thickening and scratching behavior, reduced the spleen-to-body weight ratio, decreased serum levels of IgE and IL-4 in the AD model, and significantly suppressed mast cell degranulation. Transcriptomic analysis provided evidence that genistein alleviated AD symptoms through the mast cell and TLR signaling pathways. Genistein markedly inhibited the occurrence of systemic allergic reactions and local inflammation; suppressed the release of beta-hexosaminidase, histamine, MCP-1, tryptase, TNF-alpha, and calcium in LAD2 cells. Mechanistically, genistein directly binding to the D127 and R226 sites of TRAM with high affinity (Kᴅ = 0.491 microM), played as the inhibitor of TRAM, a key molecule in the TLR signaling pathway in mast cells, thereby suppressing activation of the NF-kappaB signaling pathway. CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that genistein alleviates AD by specifically targeting the D127 and R226 sites of TRAM to inhibit mast cell activation via the PLCgamma1-IKKbeta-NF-kappaB pathway. This work elucidates a novel pharmacological mechanism of a natural compound and identifies TRAM as a promising new therapeutic target for allergic inflammatory diseases, highlighting the value of natural products in developing targeted immunomodulatory therapies.
abstract_zh: 背景：特应性皮炎（AD）是一种由肥大细胞驱动的炎症性疾病，治疗选择有限。本研究旨在探讨天然化合物金雀异黄酮（genistein）对抗AD的治疗潜力及其机制。目的：我们研究了金雀异黄酮治疗特应性皮炎的疗效及其通过肥大细胞释放细胞因子的潜在免疫机制。方法：我们采用了MC903诱导的小鼠AD模型和LAD2人肥大细胞。评估包括行为学评估、血清学、组织病理学、肥大细胞脱颗粒实验、RNA-seq、分子对接、表面等离子体共振（SPR）、通路分析，以及通过TRAM突变和拯救实验进行的功能验证。结果：金雀异黄酮减轻了耳增厚和抓挠行为，降低了AD模型中的脾脏与体重比，减少了血清IgE和IL-4水平，并显著抑制了肥大细胞脱颗粒。转录组分析提供了证据表明，金雀异黄酮通过肥大细胞和TLR信号通路缓解了AD症状。金雀异黄酮显著抑制了系统性过敏反应和局部炎症的发生；抑制了LAD2细胞中β-己糖胺酶、组胺、MCP-1、类胰蛋白酶、TNF-α和钙的释放。机制上，金雀异黄酮以高亲和力（Kᴅ = 0.491微摩尔）直接结合TRAM的D127和R226位点，作为TRAM（肥大细胞TLR信号通路中的关键分子）的抑制剂，从而抑制NF-kappaB信号通路的激活。结论：我们的研究结果表明，金雀异黄酮通过特异性靶向TRAM的D127和R226位点，经PLCgamma1-IKKbeta-NF-kappaB通路抑制肥大细胞活化，从而缓解AD。这项工作阐明了一种天然化合物的新型药理学机制，并将TRAM确定为过敏性炎症疾病的一个有前景的新治疗靶点，突显了天然产物在开发靶向免疫调节疗法中的价值。
